caption:
Both paths get people hired later. They teach very different things.

Freelancing teaches you clients, deadlines, pricing and shipping on your own. The catch: no code review, no senior to learn from, and income that changes every month.

A first job teaches you how a real codebase, a team and production work. The catch: slower money and less say in what you build.

Some people do both: a job, plus one small client on weekends.

What would you pick, and what decides it for you: money, learning or freedom?
